## What's this?

* Easy-access ONS regional GVA by SIC sector data: ITL2 & 3 geographies, SIC 2-digit, Section and Production/Construction/Services, 1998 to latest
* Same for BRES (the Business Register and Employment Survey) region-by-sector job count data, with extra-bonus higher accuracy values. 2015 to latest.
* Those two linked together into single GVA/jobcount datasets (so 2015 to latest)

### Why?

* The ONS publish **regional GVA data for the UK**, covering a range of SIC sectors (2022 is the latest available year at time of writing - the [data's here](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/grossvalueaddedgva/datasets/nominalandrealregionalgrossvalueaddedbalancedbyindustry)). But it's a faff to extract data from the excel sheets, especially for use in R or similar.
* This page **provides easy-to-access copies from that dataset**, with each useful dataset in its own CSV. It'll be **updated when the latest GVA data comes out.**
* This data also feeds into other tools/code on this website like sector analysis, GVA gap analysis. (See left-hand bar.)

### Also:

* **UK regional/sectoral job count data** is available via BRES (the Business Register and Employment Survey) [on NOMIS](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/bres), but again not in the most easily-useable form. (E.g. the website's query form will separate out different fields into their own chunk in the file.)
* It's also possible to extract more accurate job count numbers by **aggregating up from the most granular sector counts** (see the related [blog post]() for more on this.) The BRES data below uses these more accurate counts.
* So there's also **quick-access versions of all the most useful versions of the latest BRES data, including previously available years**.

### Also also:

* It's useful to have **both regional GVA and job count values combined** (for e.g. GVA per job analysis, or to have gva and job analysis using the same SIC categories and places) - this page also has **linked GVA and job count data**. 
* There are several wrinkles with this data to get them to play nicely together that anyone using should be aware of - **see details below.**
* Or for even more horrific detail, see [this blog post]() on what the code's doing and what data shaping choices have gone into the GVA / BRES join. Any thoughts on things I've stuffed up or that could be improved, let me know in the [github issues](https://github.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/issues).
* The blog post also **explains details you may need if new to this data**, like the difference between Current Prices and Chained Volume prices (and why each has to be treated very differently in analysis e.g. don't sum chained volume...)


## Automate!

**Every step - from downloading the data to creating the link tables below - is automated.**

Making data processing like this as **automated and repeatable as possible** makes it **as open and useable as possible**. As soon as new GVA or BRES data comes out, [code from the repo](https://github.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/tree/gh-pages/prepcode) can be re-run painlessly[^1]. (Other datasets and linking will be added to this process.)

[^1]: Hah. Hopefully. We'll see what else changes...

## GET THE DATA --->

* **Use the links below** to access CSVs (and RDSs for the larger BRES files, R's own compressed object format).
* These are all in the [github repo data folder](https://github.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/tree/gh-pages/data) in separate subfolders - see below for more download options using github.

### REGIONAL GVA

```{r create-download-table-regionalGVA, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#Set GitHub base URL
base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/refs/heads/gh-pages/data/regionalGVA/"

#list files
files <- list.files(path = "data/regionalGVA", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = FALSE)

#Filter down to ones we want initially
#Add in related others when making the link text
files <-files[qg('long',files)]
files <-files[!qg('imputed',files)]
files <-files[qg('current',files)]


#Define the row and column terms.
row_terms <- c("3GROUPS", "SIC_SECTION", "SIC_2DIGIT")
col_terms <- c("ITL2", "ITL3")

#Create an empty data frame to store links.
#Use row_terms as row names and col_terms as column names.
download_links <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(row_terms), ncol = length(col_terms),
                         dimnames = list(row_terms, col_terms))
download_links <- as.data.frame(download_links)

#Populate the table by searching for files that contain both the column and row keywords.
for (row in row_terms) {
  for (col in col_terms) {
    # Use stringr's str_detect to filter file names for both patterns (case-insensitive)
    matching_files <- files[
      str_detect(files, fixed(col, ignore_case = TRUE)) &
      str_detect(files, fixed(row, ignore_case = TRUE))
    ]
    
    if (length(matching_files) > 0) {
      # If multiple files match, take the first one:
      file_name <- matching_files[1]
      
      # Build the full URLs (base + file name)
      #FOR LONG, WIDE, CP AND CV together
      #Long CP is orig
      full_url_long_CP <- paste0(base_url, file_name)
      
      #Stick wide version in, CP
      full_url_wide_CP <- gsub('LONG','WIDE',full_url_long_CP) 
      
      #Long CV
      full_url_long_CV <- gsub('currentprices','chainedvolume',full_url_long_CP) 
      
      #Wide CV
      full_url_wide_CV <- gsub('currentprices','chainedvolume',full_url_wide_CP) 
      
      # Create markdown link
      # download_links[row, col] <- paste0(
      #   ""
      # )
      
      download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[long CP](%s), [wide CP](%s) -- [long CV](%s), [wide CV](%s)", 
                                          full_url_long_CP, 
                                          full_url_wide_CP,
                                          full_url_long_CV, 
                                          full_url_wide_CV
                                          )
      
      # download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[%s](%s)", file_name, full_url)
      # download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[long](%s)", full_url)
      
      
      
    } else {
      download_links[row, col] <- "Not found"
    }
  }
}

#Render
#escape = FALSE so that markdown in the cells (the links) is rendered correctly.
kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "")
# kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "Download Links for ITL2 and ITL3 Files")


```

### BRES JOB COUNT DATA (with tweaks)



```{r create-download-table-BRESdata, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#Set GitHub base URL
base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/refs/heads/gh-pages/data/BRES/separate_SIC_types_summedfrom5digitSIC/"

#list files
files <- list.files(path = "data/BRES/separate_SIC_types_summedfrom5digitSIC", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = FALSE)

#Filter down to ones we want initially
#Add in related others when making the link text
files <-files[qg('fulltime',files)]


#Define the row and column terms.
#No SIC 2 digit data here - user can just remove that row
row_terms <- c("3GROUPS", "SIC_SECTION", "SIC_2DIGIT")
col_terms <- c("level2asofJan2021", "level3asofJan2021", "nuts2016level2", "nuts2016level3")

#Create an empty data frame to store links.
#Use row_terms as row names and col_terms as column names.
download_links <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(row_terms), ncol = length(col_terms),
                         dimnames = list(row_terms, col_terms))
download_links <- as.data.frame(download_links)

#Populate the table by searching for files that contain both the column and row keywords.
for (row in row_terms) {
  for (col in col_terms) {
    # Use stringr's str_detect to filter file names for both patterns (case-insensitive)
    matching_files <- files[
      str_detect(files, fixed(col, ignore_case = TRUE)) &
      str_detect(files, fixed(row, ignore_case = TRUE))
    ]
    
    if (length(matching_files) > 0) {
      # If multiple files match, take the first one:
      file_name <- matching_files[1]
      
      # Build the full URLs (base + file name)
      #Full time by default
      full_url_FT <- paste0(base_url, file_name)
      
      #Tweak to get PT link
      full_url_PT <- gsub('2_Full','3_Part',full_url_FT) 
      
      #Tweak to get "in employment" link
      full_url_emp <- gsub('2_Fulltimeemployees','4_Employment',full_url_FT) 
      
      
      # Create markdown link
      # download_links[row, col] <- paste0(
      #   ""
      # )
      
      download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[Full time](%s), [Part time](%s), [In emp](%s)", 
                                          full_url_FT, 
                                          full_url_PT, 
                                          full_url_emp 
                                          )
      
      # download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[%s](%s)", file_name, full_url)
      # download_links[row, col] <- sprintf("[long](%s)", full_url)
      
      
      
    } else {
      download_links[row, col] <- "Not found"
    }
  }
}

#Render
#escape = FALSE so that markdown in the cells (the links) is rendered correctly.
kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "")
# kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "Download Links for ITL2 and ITL3 Files")


```




### COMBINED GVA + BRES JOB COUNT DATA

Which has to exclude imputed rent...


```{r create-download-table-comboexir, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ```{r create-download-table-combo}

#Set GitHub base URL
base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/refs/heads/gh-pages/data/regionalGVA_plus_BRESjobcounts/"

#list files
files <- list.files(path = "data/regionalGVA_plus_BRESjobcounts", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = FALSE)

#Filter down to ones we want initially
#Add in related others when making the link text
# files <-files[qg('currentprices',files)]
# files <-files[qg('MINUSimputed',files)]


#Define the row and column terms.
#No SIC 2 digit data here - user can just remove the exc. imputed rent version themselves
row_terms <- c("3GROUPS", "SIC_SECTION","SIC_2DIGIT")
col_terms <- c("ITL2", "ITL3")

#Create an empty data frame to store links.
#Use row_terms as row names and col_terms as column names.
download_links <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(row_terms), ncol = length(col_terms),
                         dimnames = list(row_terms, col_terms))
download_links <- as.data.frame(download_links)

#Populate the table by searching for files that contain both the column and row keywords.
for (row in row_terms) {
  for (col in col_terms) {
    # Use stringr's str_detect to filter file names for both patterns (case-insensitive)
    matching_files <- files[
      str_detect(files, fixed(col, ignore_case = TRUE)) &
      str_detect(files, fixed(row, ignore_case = TRUE))
    ]
    
    if (length(matching_files) > 0) {
      
      # If multiple files match, we have both CV and CP, add both to link
      
      # cat("filename length:", length(matching_files),"\n")
      
      #Create full markdown text for each here, combine below
      full_url_1 <- sprintf("[CP](%s)",paste0(base_url, matching_files[1]))
      
      # full_url_cv <- gsub('currentprices','chainedvolume',full_url_cp) 
      
      #If just one file, second is empty, no CV, leave a blank
      full_url_2 <- if_else(
        length(matching_files) == 2,
        sprintf("[CV](%s)",paste0(base_url, matching_files[2])),
        " -- "
      )
      
      download_links[row, col] <- paste0(
        full_url_1, 
        ", ", 
        full_url_2
      )                                    
      
    } else {
      download_links[row, col] <- " ---- "
    }
  }
}

#Render
#escape = FALSE so that markdown in the cells (the links) is rendered correctly.
kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "")
# kable(download_links, escape = FALSE, caption = "Download Links for ITL2 and ITL3 Files")


```









## Other ways to get the data -->

(For the original ONS / NOMIS datasets, see the links at the top of this page.)

* Look in [the data folder](https://github.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools/tree/gh-pages/data) on the repo - there are separate subfolders for each group of data. Details for each of those **are explained below.**
* Github has 4 options to access/download the files: download a single CSV, download the whole thing, get raw data (and its URL), copy to clipboard. 
* So e.g. **after clicking on a CSV** there are **three small buttons in the top right that look like this**:

![](miscimages/github_downloadbuttons.png)

* **Use 'raw'** to get the URL for raw CSV data (to e.g. get directly from URL in code)
* The **rightmost button** will download the CSV.
* The **middle button** will copy the data to the clipboard.

* **To get ALL the data in one go:** download (or [clone](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/cloning-a-repository)) the entire repo. To download - see the **green "CODE" button** on [the main page](https://github.com/DanOlner/RegionalEconomicTools)? Use that for the 'download ZIP' option, then look in the data folder after unzipping.
